questions.question: In a sample of 200 students, 80 prefer in-person classes. What is p̂?
The standard error of a sample proportion decreases when...
options: x increases but n stays fixed
questions.explanation: SE = √[p(1−p)/n], so a bigger sample gives a smaller SE.

questions.question: 810 of 1,500 voters support a bill. What is the SE of p̂?
With SE = 0.0129, what is the approximate 95% margin of error?
A sample has n = 400 and p̂ = 0.02 (8 successes). Does it satisfy the success-failure condition (≥ 10 each)?
options: No, because n p̂ = 8 is below 10
No, because n is too small
questions.explanation: The expected number of successes is only 8, below 10, so the normal model is shaky.
